currentContext.business: DSIL is a public limited company domiciled in India, incorporated in 1993, primarily engaged in the manufacture of sugar and allied products. Unclaimed dividends are tracked and remitted to the Investor Education and Protection Fund on the statutory seven-year cycle under Section 125, with periodic reminders sent to shareholders so that neither dividends nor the underlying shares are transferred to the IEPF Authority; no shares are lying in the Equity Suspense Account. currentContext.expansion: The routed sections disclose no capex or expansion PLAN. Read in full, the Corporate Overview, Directors' Report and related-party annexures describe an existing, unchanged asset base and contain no new project, no capacity addition, no debottlenecking, no commissioning or ramp timeline, and no capex outlay - and no crushing (TCD), distillery (KLPD) or cogeneration (MW) capacity figure is stated anywhere in this text. What the text does establish is the footprint: DSIL describes itself as an integrated conglomerate primarily engaged in the manufacture of sugar and allied products, today a multi-faceted, fast growing industrial group with strong presence in diversified fields such as sugar manufacturing, power and ethanol/industrial alcohol production. It operates three sugar manufacturing units - Dwarikesh Nagar (DN) and Dwarikesh Puram (DP) in Bijnor District, Uttar Pradesh, and Dwarikesh Dham (DD) in Bareilly District, Uttar Pradesh - each of which also contributes to the cogeneration division that sold power during the year, alongside a distillery operation producing industrial alcohol from B-heavy molasses generated across all sugar units. The year's narrative is one of lower utilisation of that existing base rather than of adding to it: all three units completed their crushing operations before March 31, 2026 (DD on March 6, DP on March 18 and DN on March 26), the early cessation of operations across all three units led to lower crushing volumes, sugarcane crushing declined by 7.51% y-o-y, and the overall performance of the distillery was adversely impacted by reduced cane crushing operations. Against that, gross-adjusted recovery improved to 11.38% from 10.94% and net recovery to 9.73% from 8%, and sugar production rose to 23.73 lakh quintals from 20.98 lakh quintals, chiefly because sugarcane juice was not diverted to ethanol during the year. The only multi-year commitments of a real-estate nature disclosed here are related-party property arrangements: the Mumbai corporate office is taken on Leave & License from Morarka Finance Limited for five years with an escalation clause at one-year intervals, premises for Mumbai operations are taken on Leave & License from Dwarikesh Trading Company Limited with an annual escalation clause, and the Company's Jorbagh, New Delhi premises are given to Dwarikesh Trading Company Limited on a 99-year lease running from June 1, 2011. These are occupancy arrangements, not capacity investment. Any capacity, expansion or debottlenecking assessment for DWARKESH must therefore be sourced from outside this bundle.

risks.risk: Cane availability and farm-yield volatility driven by weather
risks.note: Sugarcane crushing declined by 7.51% y-o-y and all three units ceased operations early. The same climatic conditions that lifted sucrose concentration - cool nights, dry weather at maturity, high diurnal temperature variation - constrained vegetative growth and lowered farm yields, so the year was characterised by higher recovery but reduced overall cane productivity. Throughput depends on a biological input the Company does not control.

risks.risk: Global sugar oversupply and a sharp price correction
risks.note: Global prices declined by approximately 17% in 2025 with 2026 averages stabilising around ~13-15 cents per pound. Production in major exporting countries outpaced consumption growth, Brazil continues to supply large export volumes, and sentiment remains bearish in the short term with limited near-term catalysts for a sustained recovery. Global production of ~181-190 million tonnes against ~177-178 million tonnes of consumption implies supply comfortably meeting or exceeding demand under most scenarios.

risks.risk: Structurally weak demand growth for sugar
risks.note: Global consumption is growing only ~1-1.5% a year. Rising health awareness is shifting consumers toward low-sugar and sugar-free alternatives over obesity and diabetes concerns, economic slowdown in some regions has moderated purchasing power, and industrial demand in beverages, confectionery and processed foods stays weak - structural shifts in diet preference, not a cyclical dip.

risks.risk: Sugar-versus-ethanol trade-off on the same cane
risks.note: Output is a choice between sugar and alcohol from one raw material. In the previous financial year approximately 36.90 lakh quintals of cane crushed were diverted for ethanol production, which impacted recovery levels; in FY 2025-26 the absence of juice diversion is what lifted net recovery to 9.73% from 8% and sugar production to 23.73 lakh quintals, with production sacrifice limited to B-heavy molasses use. Whichever way the diversion decision goes, one revenue stream is given up for the other.

risks.risk: Distillery earnings tethered to cane crushing volumes
risks.note: The overall performance of the distillery was adversely impacted by reduced cane crushing operations. A weak cane year transmits directly into the alcohol business through lower molasses feedstock, so the integrated model concentrates rather than diversifies the cane risk.

risks.risk: Geographic concentration of the entire asset base in Uttar Pradesh
risks.note: The Company operates three sugar mills and two distillery units, all in Uttar Pradesh, with the registered office at Dwarikesh Nagar, Bijnor. A single state's weather, cane pricing policy and crop cycle drive the whole portfolio; there is no geographic hedge across cane-growing regions.

risks.risk: Dependence on natural resources and rural ecosystems
risks.note: The sugar industry is intrinsically dependent on natural resources and rural ecosystems, which necessitates a measured and responsible approach to business operations. This exposes the Company to water availability, effluent-compliance and agricultural-ecosystem risk in operations involving process heating, distillation and large-volume water use.

risks.risk: Sole primary raw material sourced entirely from local farmers
risks.note: Sugarcane, the primary raw material, is sourced entirely from local farmers. Cane development, farmer relationships and command-area productivity are therefore the single point of dependence for sugar, cogeneration and distillery output alike, with no alternative feedstock disclosed.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Integrated sugar-power-ethanol chain: bagasse feeds cogeneration and B-heavy molasses feeds the distilleries, so by-products of sugar manufacture are monetised within the group rather than sold away
- Strong external credit standing, with a long-term credit rating of (ICRA) AA- and retention of the highest short-term rating of A1+ from ICRA for its commercial paper programme
- Payment discipline with cane growers: dues are consistently cleared ahead of schedule and all payments for cane procured during Sugar Season 2025-26 have been fully settled
- Deleveraging track record: the term loan availed for the DN distillery project was fully repaid during the fiscal year, all instalments are serviced promptly as they fall due and term loans carry subsidised rates of interest
- Cane-development capability in the command area through subsidised distribution of high-yielding improved cane seed varieties, awareness campaigns, farmer education programmes and targeted training
- Operating improvement delivered in a weak cane year: gross-adjusted recovery improved to 11.38% from 10.94% and net recovery to 9.73% from 8%, with recovery rates improving across all three units
- Flexibility in quota management: an export quota that was not economically viable to ship directly was swapped with coastal-region mills in exchange for their domestic release quota
- Listed on both the National Stock Exchange of India and the Bombay Stock Exchange

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Sugar price volatility; delayed ethanol subsidy disbursements; monsoon impact on sugarcane yield; regulatory changes in ethanol pricing

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Company has secured long-term power purchase agreements at premium rates, turning surplus power into a stable cash flow stream unrelated to sugar cycles

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Regulation] Government measures cited include "the imposition of stock holding limits on traders and dealers, along with a warning of punitive action against sugar mills that fail to sell their entire monthly release quota", with further measures under consideration to even out supply.
- [Sector supply] SS 2025-26 net sugar production achieved so far is "around 276 lakh tons", with the season expected to conclude at "approximately 280 lakh tons"; after exports of "around 7 lakh tons", closing stock is estimated at "nearly two months' domestic consumption".
- [Sector price] Ex-factory sugar prices "averaged around Rs4,000 per quintal during FY 2025-26" and are "currently ruling in the range of Rs4,200-4,300 per quintal", with the deck expecting prices to "remain firm in the near term".
- [Agronomy risk] UP cane area is "estimated to have declined marginally" though red rot impact on the Co 0238 variety "has largely receded", the variety "having been substantially replaced by newer, disease-resistant varieties"; separately "The possibility of an El Nino weather pattern poses a key risk to sugarcane production during Sugar Season 2026-27 in India", more pronounced in Maharashtra and the southern states.
- [Leadership] Founder and Promoter / Executive Chairman G. R. Morarka; Managing Directors Vijay S. Banka (CA, with the company since 2007) and B. J. Maheshwari (MD, CS cum CCO, with the company since 1994); CFO Sunil Kumar Goel; Wholetime Director Priyanka Morarka.
